# Variable-density barycentric selection

This is a weighted extension of the audited density-selection mechanism.
It is not an OC theorem. In particular the final section identifies a
possible surface-measure application whose geometric hypothesis must
still be proved in each application.

## 1. Statement

Let d>=1 and let gamma_i, 1<=i<=k, be compact positive measures of common
mass M on finite-base spaces P_i times R^d. Here P_i are finite subsets
of one Euclidean base space. Let lambda_i>0 sum to one, and let
P=sum_i lambda_i P_i. Write sigma_Q for counting measure on a finite
base Q times d-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

Suppose gamma_i<=f_i sigma_Pi, where the f_i are nonnegative finite
Borel functions on the compact marginal supports K_i. Let g be a
nonnegative extended-valued Borel function on the compact possible-output set
K=sum_i lambda_i K_i, with integral_K g d sigma_P finite. Suppose
there are Borel sets E_i subset K_i of full gamma_i measure such that
for every tuple w_i in E_i with every f_i(w_i)>0,

    g(sum_i lambda_i w_i)
      >= (sum_i lambda_i f_i(w_i)^(-1/d))^(-d).       (1)

Then for every old fixed-marginal coupling pi_0 there is a coupling pi
of the SAME marginals whose barycentric output rho satisfies

    rho_pi0 <=_cx rho,       rho <= g sigma_P.        (2)

Convex order tests every finite convex function of the full ambient
coordinates. No integer-output assertion follows unless all the allowed
product base tuples have integer barycenters. Empty mass is trivial.

## 2. A weighted area estimate

Maximize a smooth uniformly strongly convex surplus phi of the
barycenter. The compact dual proof in the earlier selection theorem
supplies locally Lipschitz inverse endpoint maps F_i satisfying

    (F_i)_*rho=gamma_i,       sum_i lambda_i F_i(y)=y

on the output support. On an output slice write F_i(p,y)=(b_i(y),T_i(y)).
For a Borel set A in the slice equality set, partition A by b_i=q in
P_i. The weighted area formula gives

    rho_p(A_q)
      <= integral_(T_i(A_q)) f_i(q,x) dx
      <= integral_(A_q) f_i(q,T_i(y)) |det DT_i(y)| dy.             (3)

The second inequality uses the usual image multiplicity, which is at
least one on the image. Borel images may be analytic and are interpreted
in the completed measures. First applying the Lipschitz null-set image
property and absolute continuity of gamma_i shows that rho_p is
absolutely continuous; boundedness of f_i is not required. Summing (3)
over the disjoint base strata, then applying Radon--Nikodym comparison,
gives, with rho_p=h_p dy,

    h_p(y)<=f_i(F_i(p,y)) |det DT_i(y)|              (4)

almost everywhere on the output equality set. Marginal domination
also shows that f_i(F_i(p,y)) is finite and positive at rho_p-almost
every point: the marginal assigns zero mass to its zero-density set.

## 3. The same slice matrix inequality

The previously proved intrinsic pullback argument applies unchanged.
At almost every density point of the finite joint input-base strata,
all base derivatives vanish and, for a common positive Hessian block H,

    C_i=H^(1/2)DT_i H^(-1/2) >=0,
    sum_i lambda_i C_i=I_d,
    det C_i=det DT_i.

At rho_p-almost every point h_p>0, (4) and the trace arithmetic-geometric
mean yield

    h_p^(1/d) sum_i lambda_i f_i(F_i)^(-1/d)
      <=sum_i lambda_i det(C_i)^(1/d)
      <=sum_i lambda_i tr(C_i)/d=1.

The reconstructed endpoints belong to E_i at rho-almost every point,
because their pushforwards are gamma_i. Equation (1), applied there,
gives
h_p<=g(p,y) at such points. Where h_p=0 the same conclusion is immediate.
Thus every smooth strongly convex surplus optimizer satisfies the fixed
measure domination in (2).

The permitted infinity values of g cause no exception to domination:
finiteness of g sigma_P makes that exceptional set sigma_P-null, and the
output's already proved slice absolute continuity makes it rho-null as
well. Compactness is required for K_i, not for the full-measure sets E_i.

## 4. One replacement for all convex tests

The set of fixed-marginal couplings with output bounded by g sigma_P is
convex and weakly compact. Indeed all measures live on fixed compact
sets, and domination by the fixed finite Borel measure is weakly closed,
as can be seen by testing nonnegative continuous functions. The set is
nonempty by the preceding optimization.

Smooth strongly convex approximations of any finite convex test show
that the maximum of that test over this density-constrained class is at
least its old value under pi_0. For finitely many convex tests, separation
from the nonnegative orthant would give a nonnegative linear combination
whose maximum is below its old value, a contradiction. Compact finite
intersections therefore supply one coupling for all convex tests. This
proves (2), with no regularity assumption on the Borel density ceilings.

## 5. Concave-power envelopes and a nonuniform face example

In one continuous affine space, condition (1) holds when all f_i are the
restriction of the same positive function f to a convex support, g=f,
and f^(-1/d) is convex. Thus submeasures of equal mass under such a
nonuniform reference measure admit the same replacement. Log-concave
positive densities satisfy this condition: f^(-1/d) is the exponential
of the convex function -(log f)/d, hence is convex.

For example the conditional probability on a generator of the cone
used in the polytopal-boundary audit is 2r dr, 0<=r<=1. In the affine
coordinate r, d=1 here and 1/(2r) is convex on (0,1]. At the zero-density
endpoint no marginal mass is present. Consequently any two equal-mass
submeasures of 2r dr admit a same-marginal midpoint replacement below
2r dr and above their old midpoint law in convex order. The exact cone
profile therefore does not obstruct a weighted replacement theorem.

For different physical support faces, one would need their actual
conditional densities, expressed relative to a common normal reference
measure, to satisfy (1) with the middle conditional density. Individual
log-concavity is insufficient to relate three different densities. No
such general surface-disintegration inequality is asserted here, and no
measurable selection over an uncountable family of normals is implicit.

# Variable-density barycentric selection

**Convex-order improving barycentric selection with variable density ceiling**

Let d>=1, lambda_i>0 sum to one, and let gamma_i be compactly supported positive finite measures of the same mass M on finite-base spaces P_i times R^d. Write sigma_Q for counting measure on Q times d-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Suppose gamma_i<=f_i sigma_(P_i), where each f_i is nonnegative finite Borel on the compact marginal support K_i, and g is nonnegative extended-valued Borel on K=sum_i lambda_i K_i with finite integral against sigma_P, P=sum_i lambda_i P_i. Require Borel E_i subset K_i of full gamma_i measure such that for EVERY tuple w_i in E_i with all f_i(w_i)>0, g(sum_i lambda_i w_i)>=(sum_i lambda_i f_i(w_i)^(-1/d))^(-d). Then every fixed-marginal coupling pi_0 has a replacement pi with the same marginals, whose barycentric output rho satisfies rho_(pi_0)<=_cx rho<=g sigma_P. No integer-output assertion follows unless the permitted base barycenters are integer.

Scope limits: The reciprocal-power envelope is an explicit hypothesis. Integer output is not automatic. The earlier selection/inverse-map theorems cited in the source remain dependencies outside this compact curated set.
